text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.5% today as oil prices jumped 3% to above $90 a barrel following U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets. Refiners like Marathon benefit when crude prices move higher because they buy oil at one price and sell refined products (gasoline, diesel) at another; a spike in geopolitical tension that pushes oil up can widen that profit margin, especially when refinery utilization is already running high at 97.4%.

The move fits a broader pattern this month—the stock is up 3.77% over two weeks as oil market volatility from U.S.-Iran escalation and Russian threats to Ukrainian energy infrastructure has pushed crude higher and kept refineries operating near full capacity, the conditions that tend to favor refiner earnings.
